markdown_report:
The best next experiment is **freshness-weighted recurring-interest pooling**: attenuate historical semantic support when its corroborating events are also old. At 10% research progress, this small extension offers a clearer experiment than another scoring architecture.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) A zero-initialized bounded residual preserves initial SASRec predictions. It does not guarantee improved ranking. (2) Distinct historical IDs can corroborate lexical recurrence. They cannot establish independent evidence, compatibility, or unmet demand. (3) Existing anchor recency suppresses old items, but witness freshness remains implicit. Explicitly aging corroboration tests whether stale recurrence contributes useful information.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Intent-aware recommendation research describes changing intent [1]. This motivates testing freshness without claiming to observe intent. (2) History-intervention research demonstrates recommendation sensitivity to edits [2]. Matched interventions can test branch dependence, but cannot identify user preferences. (3) Sampled evaluation can change model ordering [3]. Training margins and full-catalog audits therefore remain separate from the pinned selection metric.

These insights organize three directions: temporal evidence, conservative integration, and controlled evaluation. A conceptual matrix connects them:

| Method | Evidence | Temporal treatment | Integration |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Learned interactions | Causal positions | Backbone |
| Starting residual | Historical lexical recurrence | Anchor recency | Bounded feature addition |
| Proposed residual | Same recurrence | Anchor and corroboration recency | Same bounded addition |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Freshness-weighted corroboration [1,2] | 4/7/4 | Originality: precise extension; potential: tests stale support; difficulty: preserves tensor interface | Originality: familiar decay; potential: may erase persistent interests; difficulty: causal support still requires care |
| Duplicate-document witness exclusion [2] | 3/6/4 | Originality: focused control; potential: tests duplicated evidence; difficulty: deterministic grouping | Originality: standard deduplication; potential: may remove valid variants; difficulty: grouping thresholds add choices |
| Fixed lexical-hard diagnostic panel [3] | 3/6/3 | Originality: combines established probes; potential: exposes confusing candidates; difficulty: no architecture change | Originality: diagnostic contribution; potential: no direct accuracy mechanism; difficulty: false negatives complicate interpretation |

For the selected idea, multiply each anchor’s existing support by witness freshness *inside* its causal maximum. Preserve denominator shrinkage, clipping, and the zero-initialized gate. Compare against unchanged SASRec and the original residual under matched training and checkpoint opportunities; reserve shuffled-text controls only if the measured budget permits.

Keep all four routes, seeds 0/42, the 200-epoch environment default, predictor serialization, and diagnostic interfaces. Select solely through pinned macro validation HR@10. Verify causal reference agreement and exported predictor parity; report support coverage and runtime. No validation improvement is established by the supplied diagnostics.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16350 ; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606 ; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045

idea.description: Add witness-freshness attenuation to the starting confidence-aware recurring-interest residual. Historical anchors receive strong support only when a sufficiently similar distinct historical item provides recent corroboration within the current causal prefix.
idea.motivation: The qualitative audit identifies outdated historical associations as a possible failure mode. Existing diagnostics establish neither current demand nor validation benefit, so the proposal tests one narrow hypothesis: aging the corroborating evidence improves the usefulness of historical pooling beyond anchor recency alone.
idea.implementation_notes: This is a research intervention specification, not an executable replacement train.py: the baseline source and predictor entry-point signature were not supplied. Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four independent dataset routes, unchanged splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200. Write every artifact beneath the trial directory. Use only public titles, descriptions, histories, and timestamps; ignore the conflicting illustrative schema for unavailable fields. Reuse the starting residual's fixed training-item TF-IDF, threshold theta=0.1, denominator offset kappa=1, anchor decay rho_anchor=10, residual bound 0.25, and scalar gate initialized to zero. Introduce only rho_witness=10 as a fixed initial hypothesis. Both decays use retained event-position distances, not elapsed time. For anchor i at prefix t, maximize thresholded lexical similarity times exp(-(t-max(i,j))/rho_witness) over distinct nonpadding witnesses j<=t with abs(i-j)>=3. Multiply this maximum by the existing anchor decay. The newer endpoint defines pair freshness; an old anchor corroborated recently is treated differently from an entirely old pair. Empty support returns exactly zero. Preserve the positive denominator offset and downward-only norm cap, and report learned gate signs. Recompute support within the retained window; do not retain expired evidence. Keep log2feats tensor-shaped B x L x D and predict_score compatible with supplied B x L items. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; view.model must be the actual trained module. Restore diagnostic module modes and RNG states. Add descriptive original-versus-fresh support mass and residual-norm summaries without calling them relevance or calibrated confidence. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py restores identical text state, mapping, architecture, gates, and pooling. Verify against a naive causal implementation, including repeated IDs, padding, empty text, expired windows, and position-preserving future masking; verify serialized predictor score and ranking parity. Match baseline and original-residual training/checkpoint opportunities and retain all categories in every arm. Charge profiling, diagnostics, failures, and all attempted trials to 43,200 GPU-seconds; do not assume the complete control menu fits. Select only by host macro validation HR@10 with its fixed users and candidates. Full-catalog unseen recommendations for five real training users/category remain descriptive. No hidden test access, external data, pretrained weights, evaluator changes, or invented behavioral traits.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset independently:
  reuse fixed training-only TF-IDF and baseline SASRec settings
  initialize scalar g = 0
  for each B x L training sequence:
    h = causal_SASRec(sequence)
    e = item_emb(sequence)
    for each nonpadding prefix position t:
      for each nonpadding anchor i <= t:
        support = 0
        for each witness j <= t:
          if item_i != item_j and item_j != 0 and abs(i-j) >= 3:
            similarity = max(cosine(text[item_i], text[item_j]) - 0.1, 0)
            freshness = exp(-(t - max(i,j)) / 10)
            support = max(support, similarity * freshness)
        weight_i = support * exp(-(t-i) / 10)
      p = sum_i(weight_i * e_i) / (1 + sum_i(weight_i))
      p = p * min(1, stop_gradient(norm(h_t)) / (norm(p) + 1e-8))
      features_t = h_t + 0.25 * tanh(g) * p
    optimize unchanged baseline next-item loss
  save model and text artifacts; export identical predictor logic
Compare matched SASRec, original residual, and freshness residual.
Select solely using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Separates anchor age from corroboration age in a precisely specified, falsifiable extension of the starting residual.
originality.negative: Temporal decay, semantic pooling, and gated residuals are established techniques; novelty of this exact combination is unverified.

future_potential.positive: Provides a small controlled experiment on whether recurrence should expire, with possible extensions to learned temporal evidence.
future_potential.negative: Persistent entertainment interests may benefit from old evidence, while lexical overlap can still reflect boilerplate or redundant alternatives.

code_difficulty.positive: Preserves candidate-independent features, the diagnostic tensor contract, and the existing scoring head.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal support computation, retained-window handling, text artifacts, and exported inference parity still require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Intent-aware recommendation survey (supplied search reference)
contributions: Discusses changing recommendation intent across visits and within sessions, motivating temporal evidence modeling.
limitations: Does not establish that lexical recurrence measures current intent or that the proposed residual improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: History-edit interventions for sequential recommendations, Scarcelli et al. (2025; supplied reference)
contributions: Searches for minimal history edits that change sequential recommendations, motivating controlled dependence tests.
limitations: Recommendation sensitivity under edits does not identify causal user preferences or validate witness-freshness weighting.

related_work.title: Sampled evaluation and sequential recommendation rankings, Dallmann et al. (supplied reference)
contributions: Reports inconsistencies between sampled-candidate and full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator; full-catalog audits and sampled HR@10 answer different questions.
